chunks: And in the narration of Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, a man said:
I said to Abū Al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: I said to my wife, 'You are to me like the back of my mother if you leave the door of the room,' and she left.
So he said: 'There is nothing upon you.'
So I said: 'But I am able to offer expiation.'
He said: 'There is nothing upon you.'
So I said: 'I am able to offer expiation by freeing one slave or two slaves.' He said: 'There is nothing upon you, whether you are capable or not.'

key_terms.رَقَبَةً: a slave to be freed as expiation
key_terms.كَظَهْرِ: like the back of; the formula used in ẓihār

ai.seo_question: Does conditional ẓihār require expiation if the condition occurs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a conditional statement of ẓihār addressed to one's wife. Imam Abū Al-Ḥasan عليه السلام states that in this case no liability and no expiation are due, regardless of the man's ability to perform kaffārah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4838 - In the narration of Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, a man said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan (as), "I told my wife, 'You are to me as the back of my mother if you leave the room,' and she left."
Imam (as) replied: "There is nothing upon you."
I said: "But I am capable of offering expiation."
Imam (as) replied: "There is nothing upon you."
I said: "I am capable of freeing one or even two slaves as expiation." Imam (as) said: "There is nothing upon you, whether you are capable or not."
